case_name: Ram Singh v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

13 October 2008
Criminal Appeal No. 1599 of 2008 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 5797 of 2007)
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
Leave granted
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court dismissing the appeal filed by the appellant and upholding his conviction for offences punishable under Sections 302, 452 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'theIPC') and sentence of imprisonment for life, rigorous imprisonment for three years and one year respectively with fine and default stipulations.
2.  Appellant faced trial along with one Sukku alias Sikku, who 1 was convicted for offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and the other offences, as in the case of present appellant.
3.  Both the accused persons had preferred appeals before the High Court questioning correctness of the judgment recorded by learned 6th Additiona
facts: Appellant faced trial along with one Sukku alias Sikku, who was convicted for offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and the other offences, as in the case of present appellant.

The investigating agency, in order to investigate the case, arrived at the spot, prepared necessary panchnama, seized the dead body and sent it for post-mortem; seized ordinary and blood stained earth; recorded the statement of the witnesses and arrested the accused persons and at the instance of appellant Ramsingh seized a knife which was used as a weapon in the commission of the offence.
Nine witnesses were examined to further the prosecution version. Of them, Shakunbai (PW-2) was the widow of the deceased and Dhani Ram (PW-3) is his son, who claimed to be eye witnesses.
issues: Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court dismissing the appeal filed by the appellant and upholding his conviction for offences punishable under Sections 302, 452 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC') and sentence of imprisonment for life, rigorous imprisonment for three years and one year respectively with fine and default stipulations.
petitioner_arguments: The presence of PWs 2 and 3 on the spot of occurrence is highly suspicious and they being relatives of the deceased, have falsely implicated the accused persons for reasons best known to them.
respondent_arguments: Learned counsel for the State supported the judgments of the courts below.
court_reasoning: Relationship is not a factor to affect credibility of a witness. It is more often than not that a relation would not conceal actual culprit and make allegations against an innocent person.
Foundation has to be laid if plea of false implication is made. In such cases, the court has to adopt a careful approach and analyse evidence to find out whether it is cogent and credible.

The above decision has since been followed in Guli Chand and Ors. v. State of Rajasthan (1974 (3) SCC 698) 1973 Indlaw SC 371 in which Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras (AIR 1957 SC 614) 1957 Indlaw SC 71 was also relied upon.
The ground that the witness being a close relative and consequently being a partisan witness, should not be relied upon, has no substance.
holding: There is no merit in this appeal, which is, accordingly, dismissed. Appeal dismissed
